verification.notes: DePaul did deny Norman Finkelstein tenure. The university said the decision concerned the intellectual character of his work and public-intellectual persona; supporters argued outside pressure and his Israel/Palestine scholarship implicated academic freedom. The causal claim that he was denied tenure because he told the truth about Gaza is an advocacy interpretation, not an established fact.

records.text: Norman Finkelstein said Israel had a government policy called 'mowing the lawn' in Gaza, under which the IDF randomly killed Palestinians to limit population growth.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Something that lives in my mind rent-free is Norman Finkelstein informing me that Israel had a literal and actual government policy known as mowing the lawn in Gaza, where the IDF would just at random begin shooting and killing Palestinians to ensure that the population didn't grow.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 44:48. 'Mowing the grass' is a documented Israeli strategy of periodic military action to degrade Hamas's capabilities and deterrence. Reliable descriptions do not define it as random shooting of Palestinians to limit population growth; that added explanation directly misstates the strategy.

sources.title: Breaking the cycle in Gaza - Brookings Institution
sources.relevance: Explains mowing the grass as periodic degradation of Hamas capabilities, not random killing to reduce the population.
